title: ‘CM Vijay’ WhatsApp call promises Rs 11 lakh aid, Bengaluru man loses Rs 1 lakh

reading.body:
This is a real-time impersonation fraud carried out through a live video call, in which a synthetic likeness and voice were used to stand in for a public figure. The deception did not depend on a single false claim. It was staged as a sequence of roles, a chief minister offering aid, a manager requesting processing fees, and a person claiming to be a CBI officer imposing a fine, each one extracting another payment. The victim's own judgment was the only check in the loop, and it was defeated by the apparent presence of a person on screen.

The failure sits at the point of contact between a synthetic media tool and a payment channel, not inside any single system. Nothing in the reporting describes a platform verifying that the face on the call matched the person it claimed to be, and nothing describes a payment flow that flagged a series of escalating transfers to an unverified recipient. Catching this would have required a verification step independent of the call itself, such as confirming the identity or the offer through an official channel before any money moved.

What is established is that a case was registered under the Information Technology Act and that police advised the public against trusting such calls or paying on them. What is not established is who produced the deepfake, what tools were used, or whether anyone has been identified or charged. The report describes one victim and one complaint, and it does not show how many other calls of this kind were made.

reports.title: ‘CM Vijay’ WhatsApp call promises Rs 11 lakh aid, Bengaluru man loses Rs 1 lakh

summary:
A 29-year-old security guard in Bengaluru named Ratikanta Giri received a WhatsApp video call on September 9 from someone using a deepfake video and voice to pose as Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay. The caller offered him Rs 11 lakh in financial aid, then had a supposed manager demand processing fees. Giri paid over Rs 1.04 lakh through a digital payment app, including Rs 5,000, Rs 18,000, and more than Rs 50,000 after another person claiming to be a CBI officer demanded a fine.

Giri refused a further demand of Rs 50,000 and realized he had been cheated. He contacted the cybercrime helpline 1930 and then approached Byappanahalli police, who registered a case under the Information Technology Act. This is the first such deepfake case reported in the city. Police urged people not to believe such calls or make payments based on them.
